query: Explain why some Qatar Airways Business-Class flights receive a non-recommended (Recommended = no) result.

per_column.name: traveller_type_segment
per_column.rationale: This largely restates the existing 'Type of Traveller' original column, offering little new analytical leverage for explaining non-recommendation. It also introduces groundedness problems: the Doha-to-London review shows no evidence of family travel yet is labelled 'family_leisure', and the JFK bag-loss review gives no indication of leisure vs business, yet is asserted as 'solo_leisure'. Some labels (couple via 'my wife') are well warranted, but several are unsupported inferences.

per_column.name: route_or_aircraft_type_exposure
per_column.rationale: A route/haul-length axis could genuinely help group complaints (e.g. long-haul seat issues), giving some new leverage beyond the raw Route string. However, the values are near-constant ('long_haul_premium_routes' dominates all five samples including a shorter Auckland-Doha leg and generic bag-loss cases), reducing discriminative power. Groundedness is mixed: haul length is loosely inferable from routes, but 'premium' and any aircraft/fleet claims are not derivable from the source text, and the flattening of all rows into one bucket masks real variation.

judge.rationale: Both columns provide plausible grouping axes for the non-recommendation query, but their value adds are limited: 'traveller_type_segment' mostly duplicates an existing original column, and 'route_or_aircraft_type_exposure' collapses toward a near-constant dominant value. Groundedness is only moderate because several produced values assert specifics the source text does not support (invented family/solo leisure framing, 'premium'/aircraft-type claims), rather than reading silence as unknown.
